summary.title: Part 4 - Handling Multiple Clients
summary.one_liner: You learn how to handle multiple WebSocket clients in Go by using a connection Pool with channels to register, unregister and broadcast messages to every connected client.
keywords: broadcast message to all connected clients
react chat app with go backend
notify clients when user joins or leaves
takeaways: Split WebSocket code into a pkg/websocket sub-package and keep main.go minimal, exporting functions by capitalizing their names.
Define a Client struct (ID, Conn, Pool) whose Read() method forwards incoming messages to the pool's Broadcast channel.
Use a Pool struct with Register, Unregister, Broadcast channels and a map of clients, run by a Start() loop so only one goroutine writes to sockets.
Channels were chosen over sync.Mutex to safely coordinate the concurrent goroutines that each serve a connection.
Pool notifies existing clients when someone joins or leaves, and the result is verified by opening multiple browser tabs.
summary.summary: The post is part 4 of a series building a Go and ReactJS chat app. It first refactors the WebSocket code into a pkg/websocket package following the golang-standards project layout. It then introduces a Client struct with a Read() loop and a Pool struct whose Start() method handles register, unregister and broadcast events over channels. The author explains the choice of channels over sync.Mutex for thread safety, and the final main.go creates a client per connection and registers it with a shared pool. The test step is to run the backend and open several browser tabs to confirm messages reach all clients.
